narrative.northStar: The Review Desk, wired for a phone
narrative.overview:
Siple's site is the PixelCI design system ("The Review Desk", documented in `pixelci/DESIGN.md`) carried over value for value, with Siple's identity swapped in. Every neutral, status triplet, radius, and shadow is PixelCI's, under the same token names. The marketing layer (display scale, generous sections, the faint desk grid in the hero) comes from the PixelCI sales site. Siple changes three things. The accent family is the app's teal-blue instead of indigo. The app's round status lamps join as a second status device for live state. And the page reads as the app's `config.toml`: each body section is one real table of that file, outlined by a sticky file bar.

The desk is quiet and utilitarian. A cool gray page, white cards with 1px hairlines and barely visible resting shadows, one accent, status as small tags with a word in them. The only imagery is the app's own rendered screenshots, light and dark, which swap with the page theme. A code-rendered terminal and real config excerpts carry the "agents drive the same calls" story. Nothing is illustrated, and no number or listing is invented.

Light and dark come from one set of token names, redeclared for dark. Theme follows the OS through `prefers-color-scheme`. `html[data-theme]` pins the reader's choice, set by the header toggle or the page's live `[ui] theme` line. A component never branches on theme. Only the screenshot pair does, and only by showing one of its two images.
keyCharacteristics: PixelCI's Review Desk tokens unchanged, except the accent family (teal-blue) and the added `--lamp-*` tokens.
One teal accent for the primary action, the selected item, and focus. In dark it is a lighter teal with dark ink on it.
Status is a tag triplet with a word in it. Live state is a round lamp, always beside a word.
Inter for people's words; monospace for machine text: table names, keys, commands, filenames.
The page is a config file: a sticky `config.toml` band under the header, one table per section, a real excerpt beside each heading, a mono link to that table's reference at the section's foot.
Real screenshots in both themes; the app window runs off the bottom of the hero like an app left open.
Release content (version, date, every download link) is fixed at build time from the root CHANGELOG (`src/data/release.ts`); the browser only detects the visitor's OS.
No eyebrow labels. A heading stands alone.

rules.name: The One Teal Rule
rules.body: Teal means "this is the action, this is chosen, or this has focus". The header's Download is the persistent primary. Inside the page body, each section fills at most one control with teal: the hero's download button, the "This computer" row, the checked theme value. Teal never carries status. A release candidate's lamp is teal because the candidate is the build you would pick, not because it is good or bad.

rules.name: The Tag Triplet Rule
rules.body: A status tone is applied as soft fill, matching border, and tone text together, and every tag holds a word. `tag--accent` is the one solid tag. It is a selection marker ("This computer"), not a status.

rules.name: The Lamp Beside a Word Rule
rules.body: A lamp is an 8px round LED with a 3px halo of its own color at 22% (24% for amber). It always sits next to text that says the same thing (the version and date). Its color comes only from its `data-lamp` value, never from a per-element class. Opt in with `data-lamp`; without it a lamp stays idle gray.

rules.name: The Machine Text Rule
rules.body: Anything a machine reads or a person copies is monospace: config table names and keys, `siple-cli` commands, JSON-RPC calls, filenames once they resolve to real asset names, and `config.toml` itself. Everything a person wrote is Inter, including version numbers and dates, which use Inter's tabular numerals so they hold position as they resolve.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Headings carry no label above them: no small caps, no table name, no category kicker. A section's config table is named in three places that already exist: the file bar, the excerpt's `config.toml` caption, and the mono link at the section's foot.

rules.name: The Screenshot Gets the Width Rule
rules.body: Chrome never takes horizontal space from a screenshot. Navigation lives in horizontal bands, and screenshots span the full column.

rules.name: The File Is the Outline Rule
rules.body: Every section below the hero that describes a feature is one real table of Siple's config. It shows that table's real keys, and its order is the file bar's order. The license, download, and promo sections sit outside the file and do not appear in the bar.

rules.name: The Window Floats Rule
rules.body: Only a picture of the app (a screenshot window or a terminal sitting on one) lifts above the desk. Site cards stay resting, and hover changes fill, never shadow.

rules.name: The Dashed Means Not Live Rule
rules.body: A dashed 1px outline on a transparent fill with no shadow marks something that is not a live object. It is used for the "Coming soon" store buttons and the aside note under the speech turns. A real control or card is always solid.

dos: **Do** take every color from the custom properties in `tokens.css`. Keep PixelCI's names and values for everything except the accent family and the lamps, so the two sites read as one family.
**Do** fill at most one control per section with teal, and keep the rest default or ghost (The One Teal Rule).
**Do** show status as a tag triplet with a word in it, and live state as a lamp beside a sentence that says the same thing (The Lamp Beside a Word Rule).
**Do** bake release content in at build time, and make the no-JS page complete and honest.
**Do** give each feature section a real config table: an excerpt of its real keys, a place in the file bar, and a mono link to its reference (The File Is the Outline Rule).
**Do** set table names, keys, commands, and asset filenames in monospace, and everything else in Inter (The Machine Text Rule).
**Do** use the app's own light and dark renders as a pair, so a screenshot always matches the page theme.
**Do** nest radii 12px, 8px, 5px from container to control to inner piece.

**Do** keep motion to one hero settle (window and terminal rise 24px over 900ms on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`, the terminal 160ms later), the one-time terminal type-in, 280ms cross-fades, and 120ms color changes. Under reduced motion everything is static.
**Do** mark "not yet available" with a dashed, transparent, shadowless shape that still reads at full strength (The Dashed Means Not Live Rule).
donts: **Don't** use indigo anywhere; Siple's accent is teal-blue.
**Don't** use teal for status, or a status tone for a general-purpose button.
**Don't** put a lamp anywhere without a word beside it, or color a lamp by anything other than its `data-lamp` value.
**Don't** put an eyebrow, kicker, or table-name label above a heading (The No Eyebrow Rule).
**Don't** show an Apple or Microsoft store badge for a listing that does not exist; use the dashed "Coming soon" button.
**Don't** add a side rail for navigation; the outline is the horizontal file bar (The Screenshot Gets the Width Rule).
**Don't** lift site cards with more than the resting shadow; floating shadows belong to pictures of the app (The Window Floats Rule).
**Don't** use the desk grid and glow anywhere but the hero.
**Don't** hard-code a color, radius, or shadow where a token exists.
**Don't** copy the known gaps below into new work.
